newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Dunloe says capital re-organisation complete.
newsitem.headline: Dunloe says capital re-organisation complete.

text.p: Irish property and investment company Dunloe House Group Plc said on Thursday that a capital re-organisation proposed last December had been completed.
Dunloe said in a statement that existing shares of 25 Irish pence had been sub-divided and converted into new ordinary shares of five pence and deferred shares of 20 Irish pence.
The company said it would not be in a position to pay a dividend until a deficit of 4.2 million Irish pounds had been eliminated.

It has therefore proposed, subject to court approval, to cancel the deferred shares and to cancel the credit in the share premium account, in part, in order to eliminate the deficit, the company said.
Dunloe said the proposals had been approved by the Irish High Court.

The company said in order for it to proceed with its development plans, the board had proposed a rights issue which had successfully raised approximately three million Irish pounds by way of a two-for-one rights issue at 10 Irish pence per share.
Dunloe said the capital reduction had given rise to the virtual elimination of accumulated losses, which had exceeded four million Irish pounds.
The group recorded a pre-tax profit of 26,613 Irish pounds for the six months ended June 30, 1996.
Dunloe said its focus of attention was on development and investment opportunities which present profit and capital growth potential respectively.

The company said the buoyancy in the property sector throughout Ireland had resulted in an exceptionally high level of activity and it believed this strong positive trend was likely to continue as the economy continued to enjoy impressive growth,
Dunloe said a favourable interest rate environment was of vital importance to all sectors, as was the controlling of inflation.
